description: Authored editorial narratives for the synthetic product-demo and filter-lab scenario. These are mock narrative-service outputs, not generated analysis or commentary on the placeholder footage. Each moment uses only evidence available at its trigger.

home.simple: {home} are still level, but {away_creator} has tested their goalkeeper twice. Keeping those shots out is keeping the game open.
home.casual: Two warnings from {away_creator}, and {home} have survived both. At 0–0, there is still everything to play for.
home.experienced: {home} have kept {away_creator} out twice, once with the head and once with the foot. The score remains level despite those openings.
home.analytical: {away_creator}'s two recorded attempts have both been saved. For {home}, the clean sheet is intact, though those attempts show a threat worth watching.

away.simple: {away_creator} is giving {away} chances to take the lead. Both shots have been saved, so it is still 0–0.
away.casual: {away_creator} keeps asking the question, but the goalkeeper has answered twice. {away} still need that breakthrough.
away.experienced: {away_creator} has tested the keeper with a header and a right-footed effort. Different routes to goal, but neither has broken the deadlock.
away.analytical: Two recorded attempts for {away_creator}, both on target and both saved. {away} have tested the keeper without turning those attempts into a lead.

neutral.simple: The goalkeepers' work matters even at 0–0. Two saves from {away_creator}'s shots have kept the teams level.
neutral.casual: Still no breakthrough, but {away_creator} has twice come up against a save. Those are the early warning signs for {home}.
neutral.experienced: {away_creator} has threatened with both head and foot. Neither attempt has beaten the keeper, leaving the contest level.
neutral.analytical: {away_creator}'s two recorded shots have both required saves. That is evidence of a goal threat, though the score remains 0–0.

home.experienced: {home} remain level without a recorded attempt. Three saves and one off-target shot have kept {away}'s openings from becoming a lead.
home.analytical: The recorded shot count is 0–4, with three {away} efforts saved. {home} are level, but the attacking output so far favours the visitors.

away.simple: {away} have taken four shots without scoring. They are finding chances, but still need one to count.
away.casual: {away} have had the attempts; they just have not had the goal. {away_forward}'s saved header keeps that frustrating pattern going.
away.experienced: Three of {away}'s four recorded efforts have tested the goalkeeper. The opportunities are there, but the breakthrough is still missing.
away.analytical: {away} lead the recorded shots 4–0: three saved and one off target. More attempts have not yet translated into a scoreboard advantage.

neutral.simple: {away} have had all four recorded shots, but the teams are still level. Chances only change the score when someone finishes one.
neutral.casual: The shots tell one story and the score tells another. {away} have had four attempts, yet neither side has found the net.
neutral.experienced: {away} have tested the goalkeeper three times without scoring. {home} have no recorded attempt, but remain very much in the game at 0–0.
neutral.analytical: A 4–0 recorded shot advantage has produced no lead for {away}. Three saves account for most of the gap between the attempts and the score.

home.simple: {home} have had five corners this half, giving them repeated chances to send the ball towards goal. They still need to turn one into a shot.
home.casual: Five corners this half, but no recorded shot yet for {home}. The opportunities are arriving; the next step is making one count.
home.experienced: Set pieces offer {home} a route into this game. Five second-half corners have brought opportunities, though no recorded attempt has followed yet.
home.analytical: {home} have five second-half corners and no recorded shot. The set-piece opportunities have not yet translated into attempts on goal.

away.casual: {home} keep getting corners, but {away} have not yet faced a recorded shot. There is another set-piece opportunity to deal with.
away.experienced: Five second-half corners have given {home} repeated set-piece opportunities. For {away}, preventing the first attempt remains the immediate task.
away.analytical: {home}'s five second-half corners have produced no recorded attempt so far. {away} have avoided a shot, but the volume of set-piece opportunities is notable.

neutral.simple: Corners are becoming a route to goal for {home}. They have had five this half, but still need to turn those chances into a shot.
neutral.casual: {home} have collected five corners this half without recording a shot. Plenty of chances to deliver the ball, but no attempt at the end of them yet.
neutral.experienced: {home}'s route to a first attempt may be through a set piece. Five second-half corners have offered openings without a recorded shot so far.
neutral.analytical: Five second-half corners contrast with zero recorded {home} shots. Set-piece opportunity and actual attempts are telling different stories.

home.simple: {home} now have one fewer player after {home_defender}'s red card. At 0–0, they must cover the pitch with ten while still looking for a goal.
home.casual: A harder task for {home}: level on the scoreboard, but a player down. {home_defender}'s dismissal changes what they have to manage.

neutral.experienced: {home_defender}'s dismissal changes the balance at 0–0. {away} now have an extra player after recording all four attempts so far.
neutral.analytical: The red card adds a numerical advantage to {away}'s 4–0 recorded shot edge. The scoreboard is unchanged, but the conditions for the closing stages have shifted.

home.simple: {home_scorer}'s header gives ten-player {home} the lead. They have made a chance count even after losing a player.
home.casual: A player down, a goal up. {home_scorer} has given {home} something to protect after a match in which {away} had the earlier attempts.
home.experienced: {home} have turned their first recorded attempt into a lead, six minutes after the red card. {home_scorer}'s header changes the task from chasing a goal to protecting one.
home.analytical: {home} lead 1–0 despite playing with ten and trailing 1–5 in recorded attempts. {home_scorer}'s header shows how little shot volume alone says about the score.

away.analytical: {away} trail 0–1 despite a 5–1 recorded shot advantage and an extra player. The contrast is finishing: {home}'s first recorded attempt has become the opening goal.

neutral.analytical: Five recorded {away} attempts brought no goal; {home}'s first has put them ahead. The 1–0 lead comes despite the hosts' numerical disadvantage.

home.simple: {home} still lead with ten players at 95 minutes. This late corner gives them another chance to attack while protecting a narrow advantage.
home.casual: {home_scorer}'s goal is still the difference. At 95 minutes, ten-player {home} have a corner and a slender lead to look after.
home.experienced: {home} still hold the lead established after their red card. A corner at 95 minutes offers another attacking opportunity with the margin just one goal.
home.analytical: {home}'s 1–0 lead remains intact at 95 minutes despite the dismissal at 74. The late corner is an attacking opportunity, but the one-goal margin leaves little room for error.

away.simple: {away} still need an equaliser at 95 minutes. First they must deal with a {home} corner, even with their extra player.
away.casual: Time is short for {away}, and they still trail the ten-player hosts. A {home} corner is another obstacle before they can look for an equaliser.
away.experienced: {away} have not levelled since {home_scorer}'s goal. At 95 minutes, defending this corner comes before their next chance to use the extra player.
away.analytical: {away} still trail 0–1 at 95 minutes despite the numerical advantage. With {home} awarded a corner, the next immediate task is defensive rather than chasing the equaliser.

neutral.casual: The late tension is in the score: {home} are a player down but still a goal ahead. Their corner gives {away} one more thing to deal with.
neutral.experienced: {home_scorer}'s header remains the difference at 95 minutes. Ten-player {home} have another set-piece opportunity, while {away} are still chasing an equaliser.
neutral.analytical: The lead has survived from {home_scorer}'s 80th-minute header to 95 minutes. {home} now have a corner, with the score still 1–0 and their numerical disadvantage unchanged.
